Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul. It is her first full-length since *JAGUAR II*, the album that helped turn her into one of the biggest breakthrough stories of the 2024 Grammys.

The long gap was deliberate. After the awards cycle around *JAGUAR II*, she enrolled at the Institute of Culinary Education and graduated in May 2026, then completed an externship at Verse L.A. while rehearsing for Bruno Mars' European stadium tour. Cooking gave her a creative routine with no chart position or campaign attached to it. She described the appeal as "creating something that I wasn't earning from."

At first, *Frequency Of Love* was supposed to lean much harder into yacht rock. Digging through the musicians who worked with Michael Jackson and Quincy Jones led her toward Toto and that late-'70s and early-'80s sound. Culinary school gradually broke open the original plan. Pasta days sent her toward Italian music, and Jamaican dishes sent her toward Jamaican records. By the end, the album no longer belonged to one lane. As she put it, "I don't know that I'll ever be a one-lane person."

"Reach Out" moves into sleek club R&B. She has said she wrote "You Hurt Me Too" in the style of a James Bond theme, while "Juicy" carries more of the yacht-rock idea that shaped the album's earliest version. "Come Back to You" reaches in another direction, sampling The Isley Brothers' "Voyage to Atlantis." "Reach Out" also predates the finished record. She recorded it around the period when the *JAGUAR II* deluxe edition was being assembled, then held it back because she believed it deserved more than a bonus-track slot. It finally arrived as an advance single for *Frequency Of Love*. The video was filmed at the Salk Institute in La Jolla, where the stark concrete architecture becomes part of the visual rather than a generic performance backdrop.

[youtube:h99lQg2zSl0]

The album title is not meant to promise uncomplicated love songs. She has said that talking about love also means talking about heartbreak and the risk that comes with opening yourself to someone. Her daughter Hazel Monét appears alongside Leon Thomas on "You Mean The World To Me," bringing motherhood directly into that wider picture. Elsewhere, the songs move through attraction, disappointment, self-love and the possibility of being hurt.

Another thread reaches much further back. "Somebody," written by Harry Warren and Jack Brooks, entered her life when she was a child watching *Introducing Dorothy Dandridge* with her grandmother. Dorothy Dandridge became such a lasting reference that she later dressed as the actress for Halloween twice. The song now sits beside the album's contemporary R&B and dance tracks rather than being treated as a detached retro interlude.

The album now moves into its live chapter. The tour opens October 27 in Raleigh and runs through December 17 in San Francisco. At the same time, the Frequency Of Love Foundation is starting youth programs around food, agriculture, cooking and wellness. Its first projects include hands-on food education and community gardens. The connection to the album is unusually direct. Cooking school changed the music, and now food education is part of what comes next.
